rv.q: They may turn on the down-home twang a little thickly, but the cast’s conviction and verve — not to mention their robust vocal skills and warm rapport with each other — go a long way toward countering the show’s generic beer-and-sawdust variety-hour feel.
Too bad that person happened to be Johnny Cash.

cn.t: Critics find this Johnny Cash tribute revue features committed performers who deliver spirited musical performances, but suffers from a thin concept, overstretched runtime, and an artificially sweetened tone that feels incongruous on Broadway.

vs.sum: The Ethel Barrymore Theatre offers good sightlines with a well-raked mezzanine and minimal obstructions, though some box seats have limited views. Sound quality is average, with some reports of less than ideal acoustics. Comfort is typical for a Broadway theater, with decent legroom in some areas. However, facilities are lacking, with only one restroom on the lower level leading to potential congestion.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
